questions.skill: Use the angle sum and exterior angles of a triangle
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Explain why an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Give a reason for each step.
questions.correct_answer: The exterior angle = the sum of the two remote interior angles
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: the exterior angle and the adjacent interior angle form a linear pair, so they add to 180°; the three interior angles also add to 180°; so the exterior angle equals the sum of the other two interior angles.

questions.skill: Prove theorems about triangles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Prove that the angles of triangle ABC add to 180°. Use a line through C that is parallel to AB. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that the angles of triangle ABC add to 180°. Use a line through C that is parallel to AB. Give a reason for each step.
questions.correct_answer: Angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: draw line l through C parallel to AB. The angles at C along l add to 180° (straight angle). The two outer ones equal angles A and B (alternate interior angles, l ∥ AB). So angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°.
